lead.observation: Relaxing only routing to independently target-assisted choices among the fixed nine finite atoms improves the joint objective and endpoint averages, but leaves almost all vessel-padding response error.
lead.workingInference: Within this frozen own-slot0/nine-atom output family on these six public histories, the missing vessel response is largely a representation restriction rather than simply a poor shared resolver or an endpoint-versus-response tradeoff. Response-only minima remain near the joint optimum.
lead.action: Do not spend the next cut on another fit restricted to these nine atoms. Test the local representation at its actual next consumer before changing the writer representation.
lead.limits: This does not exclude another dictionary, another non-neural program family, a consumer-relative code or a different representation. It does not establish a target-free source resolver, useful continuation, generalization or pixels.

finiteMathematics.fixedFamily: Accepted104 own H0/packet and 14-atom slot0 replay; fixed nine FP32 slot1 atoms. All six previously public targets are admitted only for this target-assisted diagnostic.
finiteMathematics.stateLaw: C_i(a) = BF16_RNE(FP32_RNE(FP64(S_i) + FP64(d_a))). The actual finite S, atoms, admission and candidate labels are frozen.
finiteMathematics.responseLaw: For pair (i,j), the retained response error is (C_j(b)-C_i(a))-(Y_j-Y_i), with the source's explicit FP64 subtraction order. It is not silently replaced by P(Y-S).
finiteMathematics.scoring: Contiguous FP64 squared norms via np.sum; separately evaluated endpoint products/add and response product/add; a-major/b-minor canonical argmin; outer component sums via math.fsum.
finiteMathematics.exactness: The minimum is a complete combinatorial minimum of the declared evaluated component scores over independent finite options. It is not an exact-real optimizer over arbitrary state vectors or an assertion of bit-identical minimization of the historical global einsum reassociation.
finiteMathematics.currentFeasibility: The current route is among the same choices. Each selected component joint score cannot exceed its current-route score under the identical declared evaluation. Individual endpoint/response terms and individual rows can still worsen.
finiteMathematics.historicalMetrics: Old-style pooled einsum metrics are separately rebuilt; small last-bit differences from component fsum are retained, not used as scientific gates.
finiteMathematics.independence: The graph has disjoint components, so the component selections can coexist. Separately reported endpoint-only and response-only minima may choose different labels and are not a single feasible joint optimum.
nonclaims: No new source resolver or target-free serving program
No fresh held-out sample; reusedTransfer is historical public data

work.retainedCosts: Historical lexical table, teacher/native traces, original consumer work, fitted dictionary and routing construction remain paid. Current target-assisted finite enumeration is research computation, not a zero-neural serving implementation.

objectiveObservations.normalizerCaution: Joint endpoint and response terms are separately weighted/normalized squared-error quantities. They are not directly comparable to unweighted case-panel relative RMS values or causal error shares.

endpointObservations.denominator: Each endpoint panel uses its matching native H1-minus-own-H0 increment; 510 learned rows exclude the two fixed prefix rows. Full512/active panels retain the fixed rows.
endpointObservations.trend: All comparable case/stratum aggregate endpoint errors improve, with substantial per-row regressions retained.

responseObservations.denominator: Within each named stratum, relative RMS uses that stratum's measured native pair-response energy. Zero-native-response rows remain in the record; pooled relative RMS is not a per-row universality claim.
responseObservations.mainCapacityFinding: Vessel-padding response-only minima are 0.9638549489660839 and 0.9657607125746586 relative RMS, versus joint-selected 0.9639720049337605 and 0.9657909307896697. Removing the endpoint penalty barely changes the floor.
responseObservations.cubeContrast: Cube padding improves from 0.8894687818400577 to 0.7924841833215754, with response-only floor 0.7924773469405771. This is a positive but incomplete representation trend.
responseObservations.heterogeneity: Cube unchanged-learned response errors improve on 323 rows, worsen on 3, and tie on 183. Vessel unchanged-learned errors improve on 142/145 rows with 366/363 ties and no worsened rows.
responseObservations.nonzeroIsNotUtility: Cube unchanged-learned nonzero predicted response count falls from 479 to 306 while error improves. Vessel padding rises from zero to 141/144 nonzero rows out of 475, yet remains far from native response. Zeroing an erroneous response can help; nonzero count alone is not success.
responseObservations.repeatedPrefix: The two vessel row9 contexts repeat the same causal prefix; they are not independent replication.

routingVersusRepresentation.whatRoutingRelaxationShows: The best component-wise use of the frozen atoms improves the joint score on discovery and reused transfer, so there is routing headroom within this representation.
routingVersusRepresentation.whatItDoesNotShow: That headroom is target-assisted; no input-defined selector achieves it here. The joint-score difference is not an additive causal partition of routing versus representation error.
routingVersusRepresentation.representationRestriction: Even independently minimizing response among all 81 pair choices leaves approximately 96.4–96.6% vessel-padding relative RMS error. This is affirmative finite-family evidence that rerouting alone cannot recover that measured response on these specimens.
remainingAlternatives: A different atom family or update algebra
A state code aligned to the next consumer
A source-derived contextual program with different internal representation
routingVersusRepresentation.decision: Do not automatically expand routing depth/features, dictionary size, training data or teacher calls. Inspect the existing state-to-consumer mismatch first.

nextCut.name: Finite native-base/own-response and own-base/native-response crossover
nextCut.status: One proposed unimplemented and unrun diagnostic; no job queued or approved by this result review.
nextCut.whyNow: The fixed-nine response floor argues against another fit in that family. Prior104 row9 has a nearly correct H1 response but poor Q/K response, so hidden-coordinate accuracy alone does not identify a useful state code.
nextCut.states: a,b are authenticated native row9 H1 endpoints; p,q are frozen accepted104 own endpoints. delta_n=b-a and delta_o=q-p in the frozen FP64 subtraction order.
nextCut.diagonalCaution: Use stored F(a),F(b),F(p),F(q). Record A(a+delta_n)-b and A(p+delta_o)-q; do not silently replace stored endpoints or assume those discrepancies vanish.
nextCut.consumer: Qualified original layer1 RMS normalization and Q/K/V projection, with authenticated epsilon, norm/weight bytes, dtype, backend and original full[1,512,2560] geometry. Only row9 is substituted; other rows are retained as execution diagnostics.
nextCut.finiteOutputPolicy: Freeze all subtraction/reduction order. Retain signed terms U,V and g=(O-N)-(U+V); record evaluated closure. The exact-real squared-norm identity over these quantities includes ||U||^2+||V||^2+2<U,V>+2<U+V,g>+||g||^2, with any finite evaluation discrepancy separately measured.
nextCut.attributionLimit: Crossed terms include their admission effects; the two evaluations cannot isolate a hypothetical consumer effect on unrounded states outside the BF16 ABI. Do not report pure baseline/direction causal percentages.
nextCut.decisionUse: Native-base recovery with own response would motivate baseline/normalization-sensitive representation; poor recovery despite the native base would motivate response-direction representation. Mixed ports and signed cancellations remain informative.
nextCut.limits: One causal row and immediate consumer do not explain all vessel-padding failures, certify future closure or establish arbitrary-prompt pixels. Historical source/model costs and new original learned projections remain paid.

findings.text: The complete finite-choice instrument ran with source/custody/typed/scalar publication consistency; no material actual-result correction was identified.
Joint objectives and aggregate endpoints improve under target-assisted routing; individual row and component countertrends remain.
The vessel response remains constrained by the fixed output family even without the endpoint penalty, so another fit inside the same nine atoms is not the most informative next step.
No new native consumer or image was evaluated in106. The proposed crossover is explicitly separate and unexecuted.
Only the bounded evaluated finite-family minimum and recorded mechanics are established. The arbitrary raw-prompt-to-image zero-neural-serving goal remains unsolved.
